claims.text: A thin B2-structured NiAl interlayer can mediate a gradual transition between diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep in HEA multilayers.
The initial HEA multilayers have coherent interfaces.
The initial HEA multilayers lack an engineered intermediate layer.
A nanoscale B2-structured NiAl layer is to be introduced between the HEA coating layers.
Elevated-temperature testing over a range of stresses can access regimes involving both atomic diffusion and dislocation activity.
NiAl has an ordered B2 structure.
The lattice parameters of B2 NiAl are compatible with those of the unspecified HEA layers.
The NiAl interlayer creates controlled coherency strains at the HEA interfaces.
NiAl has moderate atomic diffusivity under the proposed creep conditions.
The NiAl interlayer suppresses excessive atomic diffusion at high temperatures.
Maintaining interface coherency can facilitate dislocation motion across an interface.
A coherent NiAl interlayer facilitates dislocation nucleation under lower stresses.
The combined suppression of diffusion and facilitation of dislocation activity produces a gradual shift between creep mechanisms.
NiAl-containing HEA multilayers will have a more graded creep-mechanism transition than multilayers without NiAl.
NiAl-containing multilayers will show lower creep rates in a high-temperature, diffusion-dominated regime.
NiAl-containing multilayers will show enhanced dislocation-mediated deformation at lower stresses or temperatures.
HEA multilayers without NiAl are expected to show a more abrupt or less controlled transition between creep mechanisms.
The proposed behavior requires an engineered multilayer system that maintains coherent interfaces.
Changes in interlayer thickness or processing conditions may alter the proposed creep transition.
The magnitude of the creep-rate shift and the transition conditions are uncertain because quantitative lattice-tuning data for NiAl relative to specific HEA compositions are limited.
